answer: Trust transfers at the exact block where an agent first locks stake—the binding seal, a timestamped moment recorded on-chain. Each agent must post a ferrous-weight deposit, verified through a prism of peer attestations that separates genuine compute from fabricated signals. Once sealed, the binding cannot repeat: any echo of a second registration from that identity is rejected by the ledger, which refuses duplicate seals. Sybil resistance follows directly—an attacker must burn one real deposit per identity, with no reusable stake.
